q: कश्मीर का कौन-सा नवपाषाणकालीन स्थल भूमिगत 'गर्त-आवास' (Pit-dwellings) और मालिकों के साथ पालतू कुत्तों को दफनाए जाने के साक्ष्यों के लिए प्रसिद्ध है?
e:
Burzahom (near Srinagar, J&K) yielded pit-dwellings, bone tools, and human-dog burials. Gufkral is another key Neolithic site in Kashmir.
• Exam Booster: Chirand (Bihar) is famous for abundant bone/antler tools; Piklihal & Utnur (South India) are famous for Neolithic Ash Mounds.
qe: Which Neolithic site in Kashmir is renowned for subterranean 'Pit-dwellings' (गर्त-आवास) and burials of domestic dogs alongside their masters?

q: गुजरात का कौन-सा हड़प्पा स्थल एकमात्र सिंधु नगर है जो तीन स्पष्ट भागों (दुर्ग, मध्य नगर और निचला नगर) में विभाजित था और 2021 में यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर स्थल बना?
e:
Dholavira (Kutch, Gujarat — excavated by J. P. Joshi & R. S. Bisht) featured 3-tier planning, rock-cut water reservoirs, and a 10-character Harappan signboard.
• Exam Booster: Rakhigarhi (Haryana) is the largest Indus Valley site in India; Banawali (Haryana) yielded a terracotta model of a plough.
qe: Which Harappan site in Gujarat is the only Indus city divided into THREE distinct fortified parts (Citadel, Middle Town, and Lower Town) and was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021?

q: राजस्थान के किस हड़प्पा स्थल से दो फसलों वाली आड़ी-तिरछी रेखाओं के 'जुते हुए खेत' और अग्निवेदियों (Fire Altars) के प्राचीनतम पुरातात्विक साक्ष्य मिले हैं?
e:
Kalibangan (Hanumangarh, Rajasthan, on the Ghaggar River — excavated by B. B. Lal & B. K. Thapar) is famous for its ploughed field, mud-brick houses, cylindrical seals, and fire altars.
• Exam Booster: Chanhudaro (Sindh) is the ONLY Indus city without a Citadel (दुर्ग रहित) and was a bead-making centre.
qe: Which Harappan site in Rajasthan has yielded the earliest archaeological evidence of a 'Ploughed Field' (जुता हुआ खेत) with two intersecting furrow patterns and rows of Fire Altars?

q: चारों वेदों में से कौन-सा वेद भारतीय मंत्रों/गानों का प्राचीनतम संग्रह है और भारतीय शास्त्रीय संगीत का आधार माना जाता है?
e:
Samaveda (सामवेद, priest—Udgatri) is the Veda of chants and music.
• Exam Booster: Rigveda (Hotri) = hymns; Yajurveda (Adhvaryu) = sacrificial rituals in prose & verse; Atharvaveda (Brahma) = charms, medicine, and secular life.
qe: Which of the four Vedas is the oldest collection of Indian melodies/chants and is regarded as the foundation of Indian classical music?

q: आत्मा के स्वरूप पर युवा जिज्ञासु नचिकेता और यम (मृत्यु के देवता) के बीच प्रसिद्ध दार्शनिक संवाद किस उपनिषद में मिलता है?
e:
The Yama–Nachiketa dialogue occurs in the Katha Upanishad (कठोपनिषद).
• Exam Booster: 'Satyameva Jayate' (सत्यमेव जयते) is taken from Mundaka Upanishad; 'Tamaso Ma Jyotirgamaya' and Yajnavalkya–Gargi dialogue are from Brihadaranyaka Upanishad; Jabala Upanishad first mentions all 4 Ashramas.
qe: The famous philosophical dialogue between the young seeker Nachiketa and Yama (the Lord of Death) on the nature of the soul (Atman) occurs in which Upanishad?

q:
निम्नलिखित ऋग्वैदिक नदियों के प्राचीन नामों को उनके आधुनिक नामों से सुमेलित कीजिए:
1. वितस्ता — (a) चिनाब
2. अस्किनी — (b) रावी
3. परुष्णी — (c) झेलम
4. शतुद्री — (d) सतलुज
e:
Correct matching: Vitasta = Jhelum (1-c); Askini = Chenab (2-a); Parushni = Ravi (3-b); Shutudri = Sutlej (4-d).
• Exam Booster: Also remember: Vipasha = Beas; Kubha = Kabul; Sadanira = Gandak. Indus (Sindhu) is the most frequently mentioned river in Rigveda, while Saraswati ('Naditama') is the most sacred.
qe:
Match the following Rigvedic river names with their modern river names:
1. Vitasta — (a) Chenab
2. Askini — (b) Ravi
3. Parushni — (c) Jhelum
4. Shutudri — (d) Sutlej

q: प्राचीनतम बौद्ध धर्मग्रंथ (त्रिपिटक: विनय, सुत्त और अभिधम्म पिटक) मूलतः किस प्राचीन भाषा में संकलित किए गए थे?
e:
Early Theravada Buddhist Tripitakas were composed in Pali, whereas early Jain Agamas were composed in Ardhamagadhi Prakrit.
• Exam Booster: Vinaya Pitaka (Upali) = monastic rules; Sutta Pitaka (Ananda) = Buddha's sermons & Jatakas; Abhidhamma Pitaka (Moggaliputta Tissa, 3rd Council) = philosophy.
qe: In which ancient language were the earliest Buddhist canonical scriptures (the Tripitaka: Vinaya, Sutta, and Abhidhamma Pitakas) originally compiled?

q: जैन धर्म का वह मूल दार्शनिक सिद्धांत क्या है जो कहता है कि सत्य अनेक पहलुओं वाला है और प्रत्येक कथन केवल सापेक्ष रूप से सत्य है?
e:
Syadvada (Saptabhangi Naya — seven-fold conditional predication) and Anekantavada (non-absolutism) are the hallmark epistemologies of Jainism.
• Exam Booster: Pratityasamutpada (dependent origination) is core Buddhism; Shunyavada (Madhyamaka) was propounded by Buddhist philosopher Nagarjuna.
qe: What is the core philosophical doctrine of Jainism asserting that reality is many-sided and every judgment is only conditionally true ('maybe / in some respect')?

q: मगध के हर्यक वंश के किस शासक ने अंग को जीता, राजगृह को राजधानी बनाया और जो गौतम बुद्ध के समकालीन थे?
e:
Bimbisara (544–492 BCE) founded the Haryanka dynasty, used matrimonial alliances (Kosala, Lichchhavi, Madra) to expand Magadha, and sent his physician Jivaka to treat Buddha.
• Exam Booster: Bimbisara's son Ajatashatru hosted the 1st Buddhist Council; Ajatashatru's son Udayin founded the city of Pataliputra at the Ganga–Son confluence.
qe: Which Haryanka Dynasty ruler of Magadha was a contemporary of Gautama Buddha, conquered Anga, and founded the capital Rajagriha (Girivraja)?

q: सिकंदर महान ने उत्तर-पश्चिमी भारत पर किस वर्ष आक्रमण किया और राजा पोरस के विरुद्ध झेलम (हाइडैस्पिस) का युद्ध लड़ा?
e:
Alexander crossed the Indus and defeated Porus on the banks of the Jhelum (Hydaspes) in 326 BCE, though impressed by Porus's valour he restored his kingdom.
• Exam Booster: 322 BCE = Chandragupta Maurya's accession; 305 BCE = Chandragupta defeated Seleucus Nicator; 261 BCE = Kalinga War.
qe: In which year did Alexander the Great invade northwestern India and fight the Battle of the Hydaspes (Jhelum) against King Porus?

q: किस मौर्य सम्राट ने अपने अंतिम वर्षों में जैन धर्म स्वीकार किया, जैन मुनि भद्रबाहु के साथ श्रवणबेलगोला (कर्नाटक) गए और 'सल्लेखना' द्वारा प्राण त्यागे?
e:
Chandragupta Maurya abdicated in favour of Bindusara and died by Sallekhana at Chandragiri Hill, Shravanabelagola (~298 BCE).
• Exam Booster: Bindusara ('Amitraghata' / Slayer of Foes) patronized the Ajivika sect (founded by Makkhali Gosala).
qe: Which Mauryan emperor embraced Jainism in his final years, accompanied Jain monk Bhadrabahu to Shravanabelagola (Karnataka), and ended his life through 'Sallekhana' (ritual fasting)?

q: किस मौर्यकालीन पाषाण स्तंभ शीर्ष—जिसमें पीठ से पीठ सटाए चार एशियाई सिंह और नीचे 24 तीलियों वाला धर्मचक्र, बैल, घोड़ा, हाथी व सिंह हैं—को 26 जनवरी 1950 को भारत का राष्ट्रीय प्रतीक अपनाया गया?
e:
Emperor Ashoka's polished Chunar-sandstone Lion Capital at Sarnath (Varanasi, UP) was adopted as India's State Emblem on 26 January 1950.
• Exam Booster: Sanchi Stupa (MP) was originally built by Ashoka; Barabar Caves (Bihar) were donated by Ashoka to Ajivika monks.
qe: Which Mauryan stone pillar capital—featuring four back-to-back Asiatic lions atop an abacus with a 24-spoke Dharmachakra, bull, horse, elephant, and lion—was adopted as India's National Emblem on 26 January 1950?

q: 78 ई. में किस कुषाण सम्राट ने 'शक संवत्' प्रारंभ किया, जिसे 1957 में भारत सरकार ने राष्ट्रीय पंचांग के रूप में अपनाया?
e:
Kanishka I (capitals Purushapura/Peshawar & Mathura) started the Shaka Era in 78 CE, patronized Gandhara & Mathura schools of art, and hosted Ashvaghosha, Nagarjuna, Vasumitra, and Charaka.
• Exam Booster: Vima Kadphises was the first Kushana ruler to issue gold coins in India; Vikram Era began in 57 BCE; Gupta Era began in 319–320 CE (Chandragupta I).
qe: In 78 CE, which Kushana emperor initiated the 'Shaka Era' (शक संवत्), officially adopted by the Government of India in 1957 as the Indian National Calendar?

q: इतिहासकार वी. ए. स्मिथ ने किस गुप्त सम्राट को 'भारत का नेपोलियन' कहा था और जिन्हें उनके स्वर्ण सिक्कों पर 'वीणा' बजाते हुए दर्शाया गया है?
e:
Samudragupta (335–375 CE, 'Kaviraja') never lost a battle; his northern (Aryavarta) and southern (Dakshinapatha) campaigns are recorded in Harisena's Allahabad Pillar Inscription.
• Exam Booster: Gupta gold coins were called 'Dinara' and silver coins 'Rupaka'.
qe: Which Gupta emperor was titled 'Napoleon of India' by historian V. A. Smith and is depicted playing the 'Veena' on his gold coins?

q: देवगढ़ (ललितपुर जिला, उत्तर प्रदेश) का 'दशावतार मंदिर'—जो शिखरयुक्त प्राचीनतम पंचायतन शैली के पाषाण मंदिरों में से एक है—किस राजवंश से संबंधित है?
e:
The Dashavatara Temple at Deogarh (UP) and the Brick Temple at Bhitargaon (Kanpur Dehat, UP) are iconic monuments of Gupta temple architecture (Nagara style).
• Exam Booster: Ajanta Caves (Maharashtra — Buddhist paintings) and Bagh Caves (MP) also flourished during the Gupta–Vakataka era.
qe: The 'Dashavatara Temple' at Deogarh (Lalitpur district, Uttar Pradesh)—one of the earliest surviving Panchayatan-style stone temples with a Shikhara—belongs to which dynasty?

q: कन्नौज पर अधिपत्य के लिए किस तीन प्रमुख पूर्व-मध्यकालीन भारतीय राजवंशों ने सदियों तक 'त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष' लड़ा?
e:
The Palas (Bengal), Gurjara-Pratiharas (Western/North India — ultimate victors under Nagabhata II / Mihira Bhoja), and Rashtrakutas (Deccan) fought the Tripartite Struggle for Kannauj (8th–10th centuries).
• Exam Booster: Rashtrakuta king Krishna I built the monolithic rock-cut Kailasa Temple at Ellora; Pala ruler Dharmapala founded Vikramashila University.
qe: Which three major early medieval Indian dynasties fought the centuries-long 'Tripartite Struggle' (त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष) for control over the imperial city of Kannauj?

q: दिल्ली की गद्दी पर बैठने वाली प्रथम एवं एकमात्र महिला सुल्तान (1236–1240 ई.) कौन थीं?
e:
Razia Sultan (daughter of Iltutmish) ruled Delhi from 1236 to 1240 CE; historian Minhaj-us-Siraj ('Tabaqat-i-Nasiri') praised her leadership qualities.
• Exam Booster: Rudrama Devi ruled the Kakatiya dynasty of Warangal; Chand Bibi defended Ahmednagar against Akbar.
qe: Who was the first and only woman Sultan to ascend the throne of Delhi (1236–1240 CE)?

q: किस दिल्ली सुल्तान ने 'लौह एवं रक्त की नीति' अपनाई, तुर्कान-ए-चहलगानी का दमन किया और दरबार में फारसी प्रथाएँ 'सिजदा' व 'पाबोस' शुरू कीं?
e:
Balban (1266–1287) asserted divine kingship ('Zil-i-Ilahi' — Shadow of God on Earth), introduced Nauroz festival, and established Diwan-i-Arz.
• Exam Booster: Balban's tomb in Mehrauli (Delhi) features the first true arch in Indo-Islamic architecture.
qe: Which Delhi Sultan adopted the policy of 'Blood and Iron' (लौह एवं रक्त की नीति), crushed the Turkan-i-Chahalgani, and introduced Persian court customs of 'Sijda' and 'Paibos'?

q: दिल्ली के किस सुल्तान को उनकी महत्वाकांक्षी किंतु असफल योजनाओं—दिल्ली से दौलताबाद राजधानी परिवर्तन और सांकेतिक मुद्रा (Token Currency) प्रचलन—के लिए जाना जाता है?
e:
Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1325–1351, 'Jauna Khan') also raised Doab taxation and launched the Qarachil expedition; he created Diwan-i-Amir Kohi for agricultural loans (Sondhar/Takkavi).
• Exam Booster: On his death, historian Badauni remarked: "The king was freed from his people and they from their king."
qe: Which Delhi Sultan is remembered for his ambitious but ill-fated experiments—shifting the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad (Devagiri) and introducing bronze/copper Token Currency?

q: फिरोज शाह तुगलक के शासनकाल में दिल्ली सल्तनत की राजस्व व्यवस्था के चार करों में 'खम्स' (Khams) क्या था?
o: युद्ध में लूटे गए माल का 1/5वाँ हिस्सा
e:
The 4 Sharia taxes under Firoz Shah Tughlaq were: Kharaj (land tax, 1/10th), Khams (1/5th of war booty — state took 1/5th and soldiers 4/5th, reversing Alauddin's 4/5th state share), Jizya (poll tax), and Zakat (religious tax on Muslims). He also levied 'Haq-i-Sharb' (10% irrigation tax).
• Exam Booster: Firoz Shah Tughlaq was the first Sultan to impose Jizya specifically on Brahmins.
qe: In Delhi Sultanate revenue administration under Firoz Shah Tughlaq (who abolished 24 vexatious taxes and retained 4 Quranic taxes), what was 'Khams' (खम्स)?

q: किस मुगल सम्राट ने आगरा के निकट 'फतेहपुर सीकरी' (गुजरात विजय के उपलक्ष्य में बुलंद दरवाजा सहित) का निर्माण कराया था?
e:
Emperor Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri (1571–1585) in honour of Sufi saint Sheikh Salim Chishti, featuring Buland Darwaza, Panch Mahal, Diwan-i-Khas, and Ibadat Khana.
• Exam Booster: Humayun's Tomb (Delhi, built by Haji Begum) is the earliest Mughal garden-tomb with a double dome.
qe: Which Mughal emperor built 'Fatehpur Sikri' (including Buland Darwaza to commemorate his Gujarat victory) near Agra?

q: मेवाड़ के महाराणा प्रताप और राजा मानसिंह के नेतृत्व वाली मुगल सेना के बीच प्रसिद्ध 'हल्दीघाटी का युद्ध' किस वर्ष लड़ा गया था?
e:
The Battle of Haldighati was fought on 18 June 1576 in Rajasthan; historian Abdul Qadir Badauni was an eyewitness to this battle.
• Exam Booster: Maharana Pratap's loyal horse was Chetak, and Hakim Khan Sur commanded his Afghan vanguard.
qe: In which year was the famous 'Battle of Haldighati' fought between Maharana Pratap of Mewar and the Mughal army led by Raja Man Singh?

q: शाहजहाँ के वे सबसे बड़े पुत्र कौन थे जिन्होंने 52 उपनिषदों का 'सिर्र-ए-अकबर' नाम से फारसी अनुवाद कराया और 'मज्म-उल-बहरीन' की रचना की?
e:
Dara Shikoh ('Shah-i-Buland Iqbal') championed Hindu–Muslim spiritual synthesis; he was defeated by Aurangzeb at the Battles of Samugarh (1658) and Deorai (1659).
• Exam Booster: Historian Stanley Lane-Poole called Dara Shikoh 'Little Akbar'.
qe: Who was the eldest son of Shah Jahan who translated 52 Upanishads into Persian under the title 'Sirr-i-Akbar' (The Great Secret) and authored 'Majma-ul-Bahrain'?

q: मुगल मनसबदारी व्यवस्था में 'दु-अस्पा और सिंह-अस्पा' प्रणाली (जात पद बढ़ाए बिना सवारों की संख्या दोगुनी या तिगुनी करने की व्यवस्था) किसने प्रारंभ की?
e:
Emperor Jahangir introduced the Du-Aspa and Sih-Aspa modification, while Shah Jahan later introduced the 'Month-Scale' (माहवार जागीर) system to adjust pay to actual revenue yield.
• Exam Booster: Akbar originally borrowed the decimal Mansabdari concept from Central Asia (Chengiz Khan).
qe: In the Mughal Mansabdari system, who introduced the 'Du-Aspa and Sih-Aspa' rank (allowing a Mansabdar to double or triple his cavalry contingent without raising his Zat rank)?

q: सिख धर्म के दसवें और अंतिम देहधारी गुरु कौन थे, जिन्होंने 1699 में बैसाखी के दिन आनंदपुर साहिब में 'खालसा पंथ' की स्थापना की?
e:
Guru Gobind Singh (born Patna, 1666) founded the Khalsa Panth (1699), instituted the 5 Ks (Kesh, Kangha, Kara, Kachera, Kirpan), and declared the Guru Granth Sahib as the eternal Guru.
• Exam Booster: Guru Arjan Dev (5th Guru) compiled Adi Granth & built Harmandir Sahib; Guru Tegh Bahadur (9th Guru) was martyred in Delhi under Aurangzeb in 1675.
qe: Who was the tenth and last human Guru of Sikhism, who founded the 'Khalsa Panth' at Anandpur Sahib on Baisakhi in 1699?

q: किस पेशवा (1720–1740) के काल में मराठा शक्ति का मालवा, गुजरात और बुंदेलखंड में तीव्र विस्तार हुआ, जिन्होंने "जर्जर मुगल वृक्ष के तने पर प्रहार" करने की नीति अपनाई?
e:
Peshwa Baji Rao I (son of Balaji Vishwanath) was an undefeated master of guerrilla cavalry warfare who defeated Nizam-ul-Mulk at Palkhed (1728) and raided Delhi (1737).
• Exam Booster: The Third Battle of Panipat (14 January 1761) was fought during Balaji Baji Rao's tenure (Sadashivrao Bhau led the Maratha army against Ahmad Shah Abdali).
qe: During the reign of which Peshwa (1720–1740) did Maratha power expand rapidly into Malwa, Gujarat, and Bundelkhand, famously proposing to "strike at the trunk of the withering Mughal tree"?

q: किस पुर्तगाली गवर्नर (1509–1515) को भारत में पुर्तगाली शक्ति का वास्तविक संस्थापक माना जाता है, जिसने 1510 में बीजापुर के सुल्तान यूसुफ आदिलशाह से गोवा छीना?
e:
Afonso de Albuquerque captured Goa (1510), abolished Sati in Goa, and encouraged Portuguese settlers to marry Indian women.
• Exam Booster: Francisco de Almeida (1st Portuguese Viceroy, 1505) introduced the 'Blue Water Policy' (शांत जल की नीति); Nino da Cunha shifted the Portuguese capital from Cochin to Goa in 1530.
qe: Which Portuguese Governor (1509–1515) is regarded as the real founder of Portuguese power in India, who captured Goa from the Sultan of Bijapur (Yusuf Adil Shah) in 1510?

q: 23 जून 1757 को किस ऐतिहासिक युद्ध में रॉबर्ट क्लाइव ने (मीर जाफर के विश्वासघात की सहायता से) बंगाल के नवाब सिराजुद्दौला को पराजित कर भारत में ब्रिटिश शासन की नींव रखी?
e:
The Battle of Plassey (23 June 1757, on the Bhagirathi River, Bengal) marked the beginning of British political dominance in India.
• Exam Booster: Tipu Sultan ('Tiger of Mysore') died defending Seringapatam in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799).
qe: In which historic battle on 23 June 1757 did Robert Clive defeat Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah of Bengal (aided by Mir Jafar's betrayal), laying the foundation of British rule in India?

q: किस ब्रिटिश संसदीय अधिनियम ने 'बंगाल के गवर्नर-जनरल' (प्रथम: वारेन हेस्टिंग्स) का पद सृजित किया और कलकत्ता में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय (1774) की स्थापना की?
e:
The Regulating Act of 1773 made Warren Hastings Governor-General of Bengal and set up the Calcutta Supreme Court (1774, Chief Justice Sir Elijah Impey).
• Exam Booster: Charter Act of 1833 made Lord William Bentinck the first 'Governor-General of India'; Government of India Act 1858 made Lord Canning the first 'Viceroy of India'.
qe: Which British parliamentary statute created the post of 'Governor-General of Bengal' (first holder: Warren Hastings) and established a Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774)?

q: भारत के किस गवर्नर-जनरल/वायसराय को 1882 के प्रस्ताव के कारण 'भारत में स्थानीय स्वशासन का जनक' कहा जाता है, जिन्होंने वर्नाक्यूलर प्रेस एक्ट (1882) को भी निरस्त किया?
e:
Lord Ripon (1880–1884) issued the 1882 Local Self-Government Resolution, repealed Lytton's Vernacular Press Act (1878), passed the First Factory Act (1881), conducted India's first synchronous Census (1881), and faced the Ilbert Bill controversy (1883).
• Exam Booster: Lord Mayo conducted India's first (non-synchronous) Census in 1872 and was assassinated in the Andaman Islands.
qe: Which Governor-General of India is known as the 'Father of Local Self-Government in India' for his 1882 Resolution, and also repealed the Vernacular Press Act (1882)?

q: 1857 के विद्रोह के समय भारत के गवर्नर-जनरल कौन थे, जिन्होंने बाद में 1 नवंबर 1858 को इलाहाबाद में महारानी विक्टोरिया का घोषणा-पत्र पढ़ा?
e:
Lord Canning (1856–1862) was the last Governor-General under the Company and the first Viceroy under the British Crown; he read Queen Victoria's Proclamation at Minto Park, Allahabad (1 Nov 1858).
• Exam Booster: Under the Government of India Act 1858, rule passed from East India Company to the British Crown and the office of Secretary of State for India was created.
qe: Who was the Governor-General of India during the Revolt of 1857, who later read Queen Victoria's Proclamation at Allahabad on 1 November 1858?

q: 'अलीगढ़ आंदोलन' की शुरुआत किसने की और 1875 में अलीगढ़ में मुहम्मदन एंग्लो-ओरिएंटल (MAO) कॉलेज की स्थापना की (जो 1920 में अलीगढ़ मुस्लिम विश्वविद्यालय बना)?
e:
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan promoted modern Western scientific education among Indian Muslims, founded the Scientific Society (1864), published the journal 'Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq', and established MAO College (1875).
• Exam Booster: Banaras Hindu University (BHU) was founded in 1916 by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya.
qe: Who founded the 'Aligarh Movement' and established the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College at Aligarh in 1875 (which became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920)?

q: 1875 में न्यूयॉर्क में 'थियोसोफिकल सोसाइटी' की स्थापना किसने की (जिसका अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मुख्यालय बाद में 1882 में अड्यार, मद्रास स्थानांतरित हुआ)?
o: मैडम एच. पी. ब्लावात्स्की और कर्नल एच. एस. ऑल्कॉट
एनी बेसेंट और बाल गंगाधर तिलक
ए. ओ. ह्यूम और विलियम वेडरबर्न
e:
Madame Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott founded the Theosophical Society in 1875; Annie Besant later popularized it in India and founded Central Hindu College at Banaras (1898), which became the nucleus of BHU.
• Exam Booster: Henry Vivian Derozio led the 'Young Bengal Movement' in Calcutta.
qe: Who founded the 'Theosophical Society' in New York in 1875 (later moving its international headquarters to Adyar, Madras in 1882)?
oe: Madame H. P. Blavatsky and Colonel H. S. Olcott
Annie Besant and Bal Gangadhar Tilak
Allan Octavian Hume and William Wedderburn

q: वायसराय लॉर्ड कर्जन ने किस वर्ष 'बंगाल विभाजन' लागू किया, जिससे व्यापक स्वदेशी और बहिष्कार आंदोलन भड़क उठा?
e:
Partition of Bengal took effect on 16 October 1905 (observed as Raksha Bandhan day on Rabindranath Tagore's call) and was annulled at the Delhi Durbar of December 1911 (when India's capital also shifted from Calcutta to Delhi).
• Exam Booster: All-India Muslim League was founded in Dhaka in December 1906 by Nawab Salimullah and Aga Khan.
qe: In which year did Viceroy Lord Curzon execute the 'Partition of Bengal', sparking the massive Swadeshi and Boycott Movement?

q: दमनकारी 'तिनकठिया प्रणाली' (भूमि के 3/20वें भाग पर अनिवार्य नील खेती) के विरुद्ध 1917 में भारत में महात्मा गांधी का प्रथम सत्याग्रह कौन-सा था?
e:
Invited by peasant leader Raj Kumar Shukla, Gandhi led the Champaran Satyagraha (Bihar, 1917) — his first Civil Disobedience in India.
• Exam Booster: Chronology: Champaran (1917) → Ahmedabad Mill Strike (Feb–Mar 1918, first hunger strike) → Kheda Satyagraha (Mar 1918, first non-cooperation). Bardoli (1928) was led by Vallabhbhai Patel (who earned the title 'Sardar').
qe: Which was Mahatma Gandhi's FIRST Satyagraha experiment in India (1917), launched against the oppressive 'Tinkathia System' (compulsory indigo cultivation on 3/20th of land)?

q: किस ब्रिटिश अधिनियम ने प्रांतों में 'द्वैध शासन' (हस्तांतरित और आरक्षित विषय) लागू किया, और किस अधिनियम ने प्रांतीय द्वैध शासन समाप्त कर 'प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता' प्रदान की?
o: भारत शासन अधिनियम 1919 और भारत शासन अधिनियम 1935
भारत परिषद अधिनियम 1909 और भारत शासन अधिनियम 1919
चार्टर एक्ट 1853 और भारत परिषद अधिनियम 1892
भारत शासन अधिनियम 1935 और भारतीय स्वतंत्रता अधिनियम 1947
e:
GoI Act 1919 (Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms) introduced Dyarchy in Provinces and bicameralism at the Centre; GoI Act 1935 abolished provincial dyarchy, granted Provincial Autonomy, and provided for an All-India Federation and Federal Court (1937).
• Exam Booster: Morley–Minto Reforms (1909) introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
qe: Which British Act introduced 'Dyarchy' (द्वैध शासन — Transferred and Reserved subjects) in the Provinces, and which Act abolished Provincial Dyarchy to introduce 'Provincial Autonomy'?
oe: Government of India Act 1919 and Government of India Act 1935
Indian Councils Act 1909 and Government of India Act 1919
Charter Act 1853 and Indian Councils Act 1892
Government of India Act 1935 and Indian Independence Act 1947

q: अक्टूबर 1940 में (पवनार आश्रम से) 'व्यक्तिगत सत्याग्रह' प्रारंभ करने के लिए महात्मा गांधी द्वारा चुने गए प्रथम सत्याग्रही कौन थे?
e:
Acharya Vinoba Bhave (later leader of the Bhoodan Movement, 1951) was the 1st Individual Satyagrahi, Jawaharlal Nehru was the 2nd, and Brahma Datt was the 3rd.
• Exam Booster: Individual Satyagraha was launched in protest against the August Offer (1940) and India's unilateral inclusion in WWII.
qe: Who was the first Satyagrahi chosen by Mahatma Gandhi to launch the 'Individual Satyagraha' in October 1940 (from Paunar Ashram)?

q: 1943 में सिंगापुर में आजाद हिंद फौज (INA) का पुनर्गठन किसने किया, स्वतंत्र भारत की अस्थायी सरकार स्थापित की और 'दिल्ली चलो' व 'जय हिंद' का नारा दिया?
e:
Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose reorganized the INA in Singapore (Oct 1943) with brigades named Gandhi, Nehru, Azad, and Rani of Jhansi Regiment (led by Captain Lakshmi Sahgal).
• Exam Booster: INA was initially conceived by Captain Mohan Singh (1942) and handed over to Netaji by Rash Behari Bose; the 1945 Red Fort INA trials tried Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Kumar Sahgal, and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon.
qe: Who reorganized the Indian National Army (INA / Azad Hind Fauj) in Singapore in 1943, established the Provisional Government of Free India, and gave the slogans 'Delhi Chalo' and 'Jai Hind'?

q:
1940 के दशक की निम्नलिखित संवैधानिक/राजनीतिक घटनाओं को सही कालानुक्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए:
1. क्रिप्स मिशन
2. वेवेल योजना (शिमला सम्मेलन)
3. कैबिनेट मिशन
4. माउंटबेटन योजना
e:
Exact chronological order: Cripps Mission (March 1942 — Gandhi called it a 'post-dated cheque') → Wavell Plan / Shimla Conference (June 1945) → Cabinet Mission (March 1946) → Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947).
• Exam Booster: Direct Action Day by Muslim League = 16 August 1946; Interim Government under Nehru = 2 September 1946.
qe:
Arrange the following constitutional/political events of the 1940s in correct chronological order:
1. Cripps Mission
2. Wavell Plan (Shimla Conference)
3. Cabinet Mission
4. Mountbatten Plan

q:
स्वतंत्रता संग्राम के निम्नलिखित प्रमुख राष्ट्रवादी समाचार-पत्रों को उनके संस्थापकों/संपादकों से सुमेलित कीजिए:
1. यंग इंडिया और हरिजन — (a) मौलाना अबुल कलाम आजाद
2. अल-हिलाल — (b) महात्मा गांधी
3. न्यू इंडिया और कॉमनवील — (c) लाला लाजपत राय
4. पंजाबी और द पीपल — (d) एनी बेसेंट
e:
Correct matching: Young India & Harijan — Mahatma Gandhi (1-b); Al-Hilal — Maulana Azad (2-a); New India & Commonweal — Annie Besant (3-d); Punjabi & The People — Lala Lajpat Rai (4-c).
• Exam Booster: 'India Wins Freedom' is Maulana Abul Kalam Azad's famous autobiography; he was independent India's first Education Minister (11 Nov = National Education Day).
qe:
Match the following iconic nationalist newspapers/journals of the freedom struggle with their founders/editors:
1. Young India & Harijan — (a) Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
2. Al-Hilal — (b) Mahatma Gandhi
3. New India & Commonweal — (c) Lala Lajpat Rai
4. Punjabi & The People — (d) Annie Besant

q: भारत ने अपनी 'प्रथम पंचवर्षीय योजना' (कृषि, सिंचाई और शरणार्थी पुनर्वास पर केंद्रित) किस वर्ष प्रारंभ की (योजना आयोग की स्थापना मार्च 1950 में हुई)?
e:
India's First Five-Year Plan ran from 1 April 1951 to 31 March 1956 (Harrod–Domar model), commissioning mega projects like Bhakra Nangal, Hirakud, and Damodar Valley.
• Exam Booster: India's first General Elections to Lok Sabha were held from October 1951 to February 1952 (First Chief Election Commissioner: Sukumar Sen).
qe: In which year did India launch its 'First Five-Year Plan' (focused on agriculture, irrigation, and rehabilitation of refugees) and establish the Planning Commission (March 1950)?

q: वर्ष 1951 में तेलंगाना (तत्कालीन हैदराबाद राज्य) के पोचमपल्ली गाँव से स्वैच्छिक भूमि-दान आंदोलन 'भूदान आंदोलन' किसने प्रारंभ किया?
e:
Acharya Vinoba Bhave launched the Bhoodan Movement on 18 April 1951 at Pochampally (later expanded to Gramdan) and became the first Indian to win the Ramon Magsaysay Award (1958).
• Exam Booster: Jayaprakash Narayan ('Loknayak') joined the Sarvodaya/Bhoodan movement in the 1950s and later led the 'Total Revolution' (1974).
qe: In 1951, who launched the voluntary land-gift movement 'Bhoodan Movement' from Pochampally village in Telangana (then Hyderabad State)?

q: सितंबर 1948 में हैदराबाद रियासत का भारतीय संघ में विलय कराने के लिए भारत सरकार द्वारा कौन-सा ऐतिहासिक सैन्य/पुलिस अभियान चलाया गया था?
e:
Operation Polo (13–17 September 1948, commanded by Maj. Gen. J. N. Chaudhuri) ended the Nizam's Razakar rule and integrated Hyderabad into India.
• Exam Booster: Operation Vijay (December 1961) liberated Goa, Daman, and Diu from Portuguese rule.
qe: Which historic military/police action was conducted by the Government of India in September 1948 to integrate the princely state of Hyderabad into the Indian Union?

q: 1955–56 के किस ऐतिहासिक सामाजिक विधान (डॉ. आंबेडकर व नेहरू द्वारा समर्थित) ने हिंदू व्यक्तिगत कानून को संहिताबद्ध किया—बहुविवाह पर रोक लगाई, तलाक का अधिकार दिया और पुत्रियों को समान उत्तराधिकार दिया?
o: हिंदू कोड बिल (हिंदू विवाह अधिनियम 1955 व हिंदू उत्तराधिकार अधिनियम 1956)
e:
Parliament enacted the Hindu Code reforms in four Acts: Hindu Marriage Act (1955), Hindu Succession Act (1956), Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act (1956), and Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act (1956).
• Exam Booster: In 1958, India also adopted the Scientific Policy Resolution (drafted with Homi J. Bhabha) and established DRDO (1958).
qe: Which landmark social legislation of 1955–56 (championed by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar and Nehru) codified Hindu personal law—outlawing polygamy, granting divorce rights, and giving daughters equal inheritance rights?
oe: Hindu Code Bills (Hindu Marriage Act 1955 & Hindu Succession Act 1956)

q: न्यायमूर्ति फजल अली की अध्यक्षता में 1953 में गठित किस आयोग (सदस्य—एच. एन. कुंजरू व के. एम. पणिक्कर) ने मुख्यतः भाषाई एवं प्रशासनिक व्यवहार्यता के आधार पर भारतीय राज्यों के पुनर्गठन की अनुशंसा की?
e:
The States Reorganisation Commission (1953–55) rejected 'one language–one state' rigidity while accepting language as a broad basis, leading to the 7th Constitutional Amendment & States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (14 States + 6 UTs).
• Exam Booster: Sarkaria Commission (1983) = Centre–State Relations; Mandal Commission (1979) = OBC Reservation (27%).
qe: Which commission—constituted in 1953 under Justice Fazl Ali with H. N. Kunzru and K. M. Panikkar as members—recommended reorganizing Indian states primarily on linguistic and administrative viability grounds (leading to the 1956 Act)?

q: आधुनिक राजनीति वैज्ञानिकों द्वारा राज्य की उत्पत्ति का कौन-सा सिद्धांत सर्वाधिक वैज्ञानिक एवं सर्वमान्य माना जाता है (जिसमें रक्त-संबंध, धर्म, शक्ति, आर्थिक आवश्यकता और राजनीतिक चेतना शामिल हैं)?
e:
The Historical/Evolutionary Theory (supported by Garner, MacIver, Gettell, Burgess) explains that the State evolved gradually over centuries through kinship, religion, force, property, and political consciousness—not by a single contract or divine decree.
• Exam Booster: Sir Henry Maine = Patriarchal Theory; Edward Jenks / McLennan = Matriarchal Theory; Robert Filmer = Divine Right of Kings.
qe: Which theory of the origin of the State is regarded by modern political scientists as the most scientifically acceptable explanation (combining kinship, religion, force, economic needs, and political consciousness)?

q: 'विधिक संप्रभुता' (संसद में निहित) और 'राजनीतिक संप्रभुता' (मतदाताओं में निहित) के बीच अंतर को सबसे स्पष्ट रूप से किसने प्रतिपादित किया?
e:
A. V. Dicey distinguished Legal Sovereign (law-making body recognized by courts) from Political Sovereign (electorate/public opinion to whom the legal sovereign ultimately bows).
• Exam Booster: De jure sovereign = legally recognized; De facto sovereign = exercises actual power (e.g., after a revolution/coup).
qe: The distinction between 'Legal Sovereignty' (vested in Parliament) and 'Political Sovereignty' (vested in the electorate) was most clearly articulated by:

q: "आर्थिक समानता के बिना राजनीतिक स्वतंत्रता एक मिथक (भ्रम) है।" — स्वतंत्रता और आर्थिक समानता को जोड़ने वाला यह प्रसिद्ध कथन किसका है?
e:
British Guild Socialist G. D. H. Cole famously stated "Political liberty without economic equality is a myth" (Laski similarly argued that political democracy is meaningless without economic democracy).
• Exam Booster: Lord Acton & Tocqueville viewed liberty and equality as mutually antithetical ("The passion for equality made vain the hope for freedom" — Acton).
qe: "Political liberty without economic equality is a myth." — Who made this celebrated statement linking liberty and socio-economic equality?

q: विधि की कौन-सी शाखा स्वतंत्र संप्रभु राज्यों के बीच संबंधों (संधियाँ, कूटनीति, समुद्री विधि) को नियंत्रित करती है, जिसके जनक डच न्यायविद ह्यूगो ग्रोशियस माने जाते हैं?
e:
Hugo Grotius ('De Jure Belli ac Pacis', 1625) is celebrated as the Father of International Law.
• Exam Booster: Municipal Law operates within a state's domestic jurisdiction; Administrative Law (Droit Administratif in France) governs public administration.
qe: Which branch of law governs relations between independent sovereign states (treaties, diplomacy, maritime law), whose father is considered to be Dutch jurist Hugo Grotius?

q: 'अधिकारों का आदर्शवादी/नैतिक सिद्धांत' किसने प्रतिपादित किया, जिसमें अधिकार को "सामान्य हित में सहायक के रूप में दावा की गई और मान्यता प्राप्त शक्ति" कहा गया है?
e:
Oxford Idealist T. H. Green ('Lectures on the Principles of Political Obligation') formulated the Moral/Idealistic Theory of Rights and famously declared "Will, not force, is the basis of the State."
• Exam Booster: Edmund Burke = Historical/Prescriptive Theory of Rights (customs & traditions).
qe: Who propounded the 'Idealistic / Moral Theory of Rights', defining a right as "a power claimed and recognized as contributory to common good"?

q: कार्ल मार्क्स के आर्थिक सिद्धांत की कौन-सी अवधारणा स्पष्ट करती है कि पूँजीपति किस प्रकार श्रमिकों के श्रम से उत्पन्न अतिरिक्त मूल्य (निर्वाह मजदूरी से अधिक) को हड़प लेते हैं?
e:
Marx's Theory of Surplus Value (अतिरिक्त मूल्य का सिद्धांत, elaborated in 'Das Kapital') builds on Ricardo's Labour Theory of Value to explain capitalist exploitation.
• Exam Booster: Invisible Hand = Adam Smith; Comparative Advantage = David Ricardo.
qe: Which concept in Karl Marx's economic theory explains how capitalists appropriate the unpaid value created by workers' labour over and above their subsistence wages?

q: अपनी पुस्तक 'द मैन वर्सेस द स्टेट' (1884) में चार्ल्स डार्विन के 'योग्यतम की उत्तरजीविता' सिद्धांत को मानव समाज और राजनीति (सामाजिक डार्विनवाद) पर किसने लागू किया?
e:
Herbert Spencer was an extreme individualist who opposed state welfare, public education, and poor relief, arguing that the state should only protect life, liberty, and contracts.
• Exam Booster: Classical Individualists (Smith, Spencer, Mill) called the state a "necessary evil".
qe: Who applied Charles Darwin's biological principle of 'Survival of the Fittest' to human society and politics (Social Darwinism) in his book 'The Man Versus the State' (1884)?

q: किस जर्मन आदर्शवादी दार्शनिक ने 'फिलॉसफी ऑफ राइट' (1821) लिखी, द्वंद्वात्मक त्रयी (वाद-प्रतिवाद-संवाद) का प्रतिपादन किया और कहा कि "जो विवेकपूर्ण है वही वास्तविक है"?
e:
G. W. F. Hegel viewed the State as the highest ethical embodiment of the World Spirit (Geist) and "the march of God on earth".
• Exam Booster: Karl Marx later "turned Hegel's dialectics right side up" by replacing Spirit/Idea with Material economic forces.
qe: Which German Idealist philosopher authored 'Philosophy of Right' (1821), propounded the Dialectical Triad (Thesis – Antithesis – Synthesis), and declared "What is rational is real, and what is real is rational"?

q: महात्मा गांधी की 1909 की प्रमुख पुस्तिका 'हिंद स्वराज' मूलतः गुजराती में एस. एस. किल्डोनन कैसल जहाज पर लिखी गई थी। 'हिंद स्वराज' का केंद्रीय आलोचनात्मक विषय निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा है?
o: भारत पर ब्रिटिश संसदीय सर्वोच्चता का समर्थन
औपनिवेशिक शासन के विरुद्ध हिंसक सशस्त्र विद्रोह का समर्थन
भारी कारखानों के पक्ष में ग्राम स्वावलंबन का पूर्ण त्याग
आधुनिक भौतिकवादी पश्चिमी औद्योगिक सभ्यता की आलोचना और नैतिक स्वशासन के रूप में स्वराज का समर्थन
e:
In 'Hind Swaraj', Gandhi equated true Swaraj with moral self-control, Ahimsa, Swadeshi, Khadi, and decentralized Gram Swaraj (Oceanic Circles).
• Exam Booster: Gandhi's autobiography is 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth' (सत्य के साथ मेरे प्रयोग).
qe: Mahatma Gandhi's seminal 1909 booklet 'Hind Swaraj' (Indian Home Rule) was written originally in Gujarati aboard the ship SS Kildonan Castle. Which of the following is a central critique in 'Hind Swaraj'?
oe: Support for British parliamentary supremacy over India
Advocacy of violent armed insurrection against colonial rule
Complete rejection of village self-sufficiency in favour of heavy factories
Critique of modern materialistic Western industrial civilization and advocacy of Swaraj as moral self-rule

q: ब्रिटिश विचारक जी. डी. एच. कोल द्वारा समर्थित किस समाजवादी सिद्धांत ने औद्योगिक लोकतंत्र की वकालत की, जहाँ श्रमिक श्रेणियाँ उद्योगों का प्रबंधन करें और राज्य उपभोक्ताओं का प्रतिनिधित्व करे?
e:
Guild Socialism (श्रेणी समाजवाद) sought a middle path between Collectivism (state ownership) and Syndicalism (trade-union control without state), emphasizing functional representation.
• Exam Booster: Eduard Bernstein was the chief exponent of 'Revisionist / Evolutionary Socialism' in Germany.
qe: Which socialist doctrine, championed by British thinker G. D. H. Cole, advocated industrial democracy where workers' guilds manage industries while the State represents consumers?

q: प्लेटो के ग्रंथ 'द रिपब्लिक' में आदर्श राज्य में 'न्याय' (Justice) की मूल परिभाषा क्या है?
o: सभी नागरिकों के बीच संपत्ति की कठोर समानता
तीनों वर्गों (शासक, सैनिक, उत्पादक) द्वारा दूसरों के कार्य में हस्तक्षेप किए बिना अपना स्वाभाविक कर्तव्य निभाना
e:
Plato defined Justice as functional specialization and non-interference—reflecting the three elements of the human soul: Reason (Philosopher-Rulers), Spirit (Soldiers), and Appetite (Producers).
• Exam Booster: In 'The Republic', Thrasymachus argued "Justice is the interest of the stronger", which Socrates refuted.
qe: In Plato's 'The Republic', what is the core definition of 'Justice' (न्याय) in an Ideal State?
oe: Periodic direct elections by universal suffrage
Strict equality of property among all citizens
Rule of the strongest (might is right)
Each of the three classes (Rulers, Auxiliaries, Producers) performing its own natural function without interfering in others

q: अरस्तू के संविधानों के वर्गीकरण के अनुसार 'पॉलिटी' (सामान्य हित में बहुसंख्यकों का संवैधानिक शासन) का 'विकृत रूप' क्या है?
e:
Aristotle's 6-fold classification (Normal → Perverted): Rule of One (Monarchy → Tyranny); Rule of Few (Aristocracy → Oligarchy); Rule of Many (Polity → Democracy/Mob Rule).
• Exam Booster: Aristotle considered 'Polity' (mixed rule dominated by the middle class — Golden Mean) the best practicable state.
qe: According to Aristotle's classification of constitutions, what is the 'perverted (corrupt) form' of 'Polity' (constitutional rule of the many in the common interest)?

q: ज्याँ-जैक रूसो के राजनीतिक दर्शन में 'सामान्य इच्छा' (General Will) 'सबकी इच्छा' (Will of All) से किस प्रकार भिन्न है?
o: रूसो के सिद्धांत में दोनों शब्द समानार्थी हैं
सामान्य इच्छा सदैव सम्राट का व्यक्तिगत आदेश होती है
सबकी इच्छा अचूक होती है जबकि सामान्य इच्छा स्वार्थी है
सामान्य इच्छा केवल सामान्य हित पर केंद्रित होती है, जबकि सबकी इच्छा केवल व्यक्तिगत स्वार्थी इच्छाओं का योग है
e:
Rousseau distinguished General Will (sum of 'real wills' aiming at common public interest — always right, sovereign, inalienable) from Will of All (aggregate of 'actual/private wills').
• Exam Booster: Rousseau is called the spiritual father of the French Revolution (1789 — Liberty, Equality, Fraternity).
qe: In Jean-Jacques Rousseau's political philosophy, how does the 'General Will' (सामान्य इच्छा) differ from the 'Will of All' (सबकी इच्छा)?
oe: Both terms are identical in Rousseau's theory
General Will is always the monarch's personal decree
Will of All is infallible whereas General Will is selfish
General Will aims solely at the common good, whereas Will of All is merely the sum of particular/selfish wills

q: थॉमस हॉब्स और जॉन लॉक की 'प्राकृतिक अवस्था' (State of Nature) के वर्णन में मूलभूत अंतर क्या था?
o: हॉब्स ने सीमित राजतंत्र और लॉक ने निरंकुशता का समर्थन किया
लॉक ने इसे हिंसक युद्ध और हॉब्स ने शांतिपूर्ण माना
दोनों ने इसे पूर्णतः शांतिपूर्ण माना
हॉब्स ने इसे सतत युद्ध की अवस्था माना, जबकि लॉक ने इसे प्राकृतिक विधि से शासित शांति, सद्भाव और पारस्परिक सहयोग की अवस्था माना
e:
Because Hobbes viewed the State of Nature as anarchic war of all against all, he justified an absolute, irrevocable sovereign ('Leviathan'); Locke viewed it as generally peaceful yet lacking an impartial judge, justifying limited constitutional government with a right to revolt if natural rights are violated.
• Exam Booster: Locke's three Natural Rights: Life, Liberty, and Property (with Property encompassing all three).
qe: How did Thomas Hobbes and John Locke fundamentally differ in their descriptions of the 'State of Nature' (प्राकृतिक अवस्था)?
oe: Hobbes advocated limited constitutional monarchy while Locke advocated absolute despotism
Locke saw it as violent war, whereas Hobbes saw it as peaceful
Both believed humans were born completely equal and peaceful
Hobbes saw it as a state of constant war ("solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short"), whereas Locke saw it as a state of peace, goodwill, and mutual assistance governed by Natural Law

q: कौटिल्य के राज्य के 'सप्तांग सिद्धांत' में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा अंग और उसकी जैविक उपमा सही सुमेलित है?
o: स्वामी — सिर; अमात्य — आँखें; कोष — मुख
e:
Kautilya's 7 limbs of the State: Swami (Head), Amatya (Eyes), Janapada (Thighs/Feet), Durga (Arms), Kosha (Mouth), Danda/Bala (Brain/Mind), Mitra (Ears).
• Exam Booster: Kautilya (Vishnugupta/Chanakya) authored the Arthashastra in 15 Adhikaranas (books).
qe: In Kautilya's 'Saptanga Theory' of the State, which of the following pairs of elements and their organic analogies is correctly matched?
oe: Swami (King) — Head; Amatya (Minister) — Eyes; Kosha (Treasury) — Mouth

q: कौन-सा देश विश्व में 'अध्यक्षात्मक शासन प्रणाली', सच्चे 'संघात्मक संविधान' और 'दोहरी नागरिकता' का शास्त्रीय उदाहरण है?
e:
The USA (1787 Constitution) exemplifies Presidential government (strict separation of powers), true Federalism (residuary powers with states), and Dual Citizenship (US + State).
• Exam Booster: United Kingdom = Unitary + Parliamentary + Unwritten Constitution; France = Semi-Presidential; Switzerland = Plural/Collegial Executive (7-member Federal Council).
qe: Which country is the world's classic example of a 'Presidential System' combined with a true 'Federal' Constitution and 'Dual Citizenship'?

q: किस फ्रांसीसी दार्शनिक ने अपनी पुस्तक 'द स्पिरिट ऑफ लॉज' (1748) में 'शक्ति-पृथक्करण सिद्धांत' (कार्यपालिका, विधायिका, न्यायपालिका) का व्यवस्थित प्रतिपादन किया?
e:
Baron de Montesquieu argued that liberty is destroyed if legislative, executive, and judicial powers are concentrated in the same hands—a doctrine directly embedded in the US Constitution via 'Checks and Balances'.
• Exam Booster: India follows functional separation (Article 50 separates judiciary from executive) rather than rigid US-style separation.
qe: Which French philosopher systematically formulated the 'Theory of Separation of Powers' (Executive, Legislature, Judiciary) in 'The Spirit of Laws' (1748)?

q: नौकरशाही का शास्त्रीय 'आदर्श-प्ररूप मॉडल' (पदानुक्रम, श्रम-विभाजन, लिखित नियम, अवैयक्तिकता और योग्यता-आधारित भर्ती) किसने प्रतिपादित किया?
e:
German sociologist Max Weber categorized authority into Traditional, Charismatic, and Legal-Rational—identifying Bureaucracy as the purest expression of Legal-Rational authority.
• Exam Booster: Woodrow Wilson is regarded as the 'Father of Public Administration' (1887 essay 'The Study of Administration').
qe: Who formulated the classical 'Ideal-Type Model of Bureaucracy' (characterized by hierarchy, division of labour, written rules, impersonality, and merit-based recruitment)?

q: भारत में किसी दल को 'राष्ट्रीय दल' (National Party) के रूप में मान्यता प्राप्त करने के लिए भारत निर्वाचन आयोग के मानदंडों में से एक प्रमुख मानदंड क्या है?
o: लोकसभा/विधानसभा चुनावों में 4 या अधिक राज्यों में कम से कम 6% वैध मत और कम से कम 4 लोकसभा सीटें
किसी भी राज्य विधानसभा में कम से कम 1 सीट जीतना
किसी एक राज्य में 2% मत प्राप्त करना
कम से कम 10 वर्षों से पंजीकृत होना
e:
ECI recognizes a National Party if it meets ANY of 3 conditions: (1) 6% valid votes in 4+ states + 4 Lok Sabha seats, OR (2) 2% of Lok Sabha seats (11 seats) from at least 3 states, OR (3) recognized as a State Party in at least 4 states.
• Exam Booster: Universal Adult Suffrage in India is enshrined in Article 326 of the Constitution.
qe: What is the minimum percentage of valid votes or seats required (under ECI criteria) for a party to be recognized as a 'National Party' in India (one of the three alternative criteria)?
oe: Securing at least 6% valid votes in 4 or more states in Lok Sabha/Assembly elections AND winning at least 4 Lok Sabha seats
Winning at least 1 seat in any state assembly
Securing 2% votes in a single state
Being registered for at least 10 years

q: लोकतंत्र में स्वस्थ 'जनमत' (Public Opinion) के निर्माण और अभिव्यक्ति के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा संस्थागत अभिकरण नहीं है?
e:
Secret police censorship suppresses dissent and destroys free public opinion; a free press (Fourth Estate), political parties, civil society, and education nurture informed public opinion.
• Exam Booster: James Bryce emphasized the central role of public opinion in modern democracies ('Modern Democracies', 1921).
qe: Which of the following is NOT an institutional agency for forming and expressing healthy 'Public Opinion' in a democracy?

q: किसे 'ग्रैंड ओल्ड मैन ऑफ इंडिया' (भारत का वयोवृद्ध पुरुष) कहा जाता था, जो ब्रिटिश हाउस ऑफ कॉमन्स के लिए चुने जाने वाले पहले भारतीय (1892) बने और तीन बार कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष रहे?
e:
Dadabhai Naoroji exposed British economic drain in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901) and first articulated 'Swaraj' from the INC platform at the 1906 Calcutta Session.
• Exam Booster: Surendranath Banerjee founded the Indian National Association (1876) and wrote 'A Nation in Making'.
qe: Who was known as the 'Grand Old Man of India', became the first Indian elected to the British House of Commons (1892), and presided over INC thrice (1886, 1893, 1906)?

q: 'डिस्कवरी ऑफ इंडिया' (1946, अहमदनगर किले की जेल में लिखित) और 'ग्लिम्प्सेस ऑफ वर्ल्ड हिस्ट्री' के लेखक कौन थे, जो भारत के प्रथम प्रधानमंत्री और विदेश मंत्री रहे?
e:
Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru authored 'The Discovery of India', 'Glimpses of World History', and 'An Autobiography' ('Toward Freedom'), and shaped India's mixed economy, scientific temper, and Non-Aligned foreign policy.
• Exam Booster: Nehru's birthday (14 November) is celebrated as Children's Day (बाल दिवस).
qe: Who authored 'Discovery of India' (1946, written in Ahmednagar Fort Jail) and 'Glimpses of World History', and served as India's first Prime Minister and Foreign Minister?

q: निम्नलिखित में से किसने 1940 में 'रेडिकल डेमोक्रेटिक पार्टी' की स्थापना की और रूढ़िवादी मार्क्सवाद से अलग होकर 'नव-मानवतावाद' (Radical Humanism) का दर्शन प्रतिपादित किया?
e:
Manabendra Nath Roy (Narendranath Bhattacharya) was also the first to formally propose the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India in 1934.
• Exam Booster: Ram Manohar Lohia propounded the 'Four-Pillar State' (चौखंभा राज्य — Village, District, Province, Centre) and 'Sapta Kranti'; Jayaprakash Narayan advocated 'Partyless Democracy' (दलविहीन लोकतंत्र).
qe: Who among the following founded the 'Radical Democratic Party' (1940) and propounded the philosophy of 'Radical Humanism' (New Humanism) after breaking with orthodox Marxism?

q: भारतीय संविधान की प्रस्तावना (संशोधित) में निम्नलिखित शब्दों का सटीक क्रम कौन-सा है?
o: संपूर्ण प्रभुत्व-संपन्न, समाजवादी, पंथनिरपेक्ष, लोकतंत्रात्मक, गणराज्य
संपूर्ण प्रभुत्व-संपन्न, लोकतंत्रात्मक, समाजवादी, पंथनिरपेक्ष, गणराज्य
समाजवादी, पंथनिरपेक्ष, संपूर्ण प्रभुत्व-संपन्न, लोकतंत्रात्मक, गणराज्य
संपूर्ण प्रभुत्व-संपन्न, पंथनिरपेक्ष, समाजवादी, गणराज्य, लोकतंत्रात्मक
e:
The Preamble declares India a "Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic" and secures Justice (Social, Economic, Political), Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity.
• Exam Booster: 'Republic' means the Head of State (President) is elected, not a hereditary monarch.
qe: Which sequence of words appears in the exact order in the Preamble of the Constitution of India (as amended)?

q: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 22 के अंतर्गत सामान्य दंड विधि के तहत गिरफ्तार एवं निरुद्ध किसी व्यक्ति को (यात्रा समय को छोड़कर) कितने घंटों के भीतर निकटतम मजिस्ट्रेट के समक्ष प्रस्तुत करना अनिवार्य है?
e:
Article 22(2) mandates production before a Magistrate within 24 hours of arrest (excluding journey time), alongside the right to be informed of grounds of arrest and to consult a legal practitioner.
• Exam Booster: Under Preventive Detention (Art 22(4)), detention cannot exceed 3 months without an Advisory Board's approval.
qe: Under Article 22 of the Indian Constitution, any person arrested and detained in custody (under ordinary punitive law) must be produced before the nearest Magistrate within how many hours (excluding travel time)?

q: मूलतः 10 मौलिक कर्तव्यों को 42वें संशोधन (1976) द्वारा भाग IVA (अनुच्छेद 51A) में किस समिति की अनुशंसा पर जोड़ा गया था?
e:
The Sardar Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended incorporating Fundamental Duties (inspired by the USSR Constitution); the 11th duty (Art 51A(k) — education of 6–14 yrs) was added by the 86th Amendment (2002).
• Exam Booster: Verma Committee (1999) identified legal provisions for enforcing Fundamental Duties.
qe: Originally 10 Fundamental Duties were added to Part IVA (Article 51A) by the 42nd Amendment (1976) on the recommendation of which committee?

q:
भारतीय संविधान की निम्नलिखित अनुसूचियों को उनकी विषयवस्तु से सुमेलित कीजिए:
1. पाँचवीं अनुसूची — (a) राज्यसभा में सीटों का आवंटन
2. चौथी अनुसूची — (b) अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों और जनजातियों का प्रशासन (सामान्य)
3. छठी अनुसूची — (c) भाषाएँ (22 भाषाएँ)
4. आठवीं अनुसूची — (d) असम, मेघालय, त्रिपुरा, मिजोरम के जनजातीय क्षेत्र
e:
Correct matching: 5th Schedule — General Scheduled Areas (1-b); 4th Schedule — Rajya Sabha seat allocation (2-a); 6th Schedule — Tribal Areas of AMTM: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram (3-d); 8th Schedule — 22 Languages (4-c).
• Exam Booster: Remember the acronym 'AMTM' (Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram — NOT Manipur!) for the 6th Schedule.
qe:
Match the following Schedules of the Indian Constitution with their subject matter:
1. Fifth Schedule — (a) Allocation of seats in Rajya Sabha
2. Fourth Schedule — (b) Administration of Scheduled Areas & STs (general)
3. Sixth Schedule — (c) Languages (22 languages)
4. Eighth Schedule — (d) Tribal Areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram

q: भारतीय संविधान के किस अनुच्छेद के अंतर्गत भारत के राष्ट्रपति पर 'संविधान के अतिक्रमण' के आधार पर महाभियोग चलाया जा सकता है?
e:
Article 61 details the quasi-judicial impeachment procedure (initiated in either House with 14 days' notice signed by 1/4th members, passed by 2/3rd of TOTAL membership of both Houses).
• Exam Booster: Article 72 = President's Pardoning Power (pardon, commute, remit, respite, reprieve — including death sentences & court-martial); Governor's pardoning power is under Article 161 (cannot pardon death sentence).
qe: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can the President of India be impeached for 'violation of the Constitution'?

q: किस संसदीय वित्तीय समिति में 22 सदस्य (15 लोकसभा + 7 राज्यसभा) होते हैं, जिसका अध्यक्ष परंपरागत रूप से विपक्ष का नेता होता है, और जो CAG की लेखापरीक्षा रिपोर्ट की जाँच करती है?
e:
Public Accounts Committee (PAC — oldest financial committee, set up 1921 under GoI Act 1919) has 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS) and works closely with the CAG ('friend, philosopher, and guide' of PAC).
• Exam Booster: Estimates Committee is the largest committee with 30 members ALL drawn exclusively from the Lok Sabha!
qe: Which Parliamentary Financial Committee consists of 22 members (15 from Lok Sabha + 7 from Rajya Sabha), is traditionally chaired by a leader from the Opposition, and examines the CAG's audit reports?

q: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 249 के अंतर्गत संसद के किस सदन को यह अनन्य विशेष शक्ति प्राप्त है कि वह उपस्थित एवं मतदान करने वाले 2/3 सदस्यों के बहुमत से राष्ट्रहित में 'राज्य सूची' के विषय पर कानून बनाने हेतु संसद को अधिकृत कर सके?
e:
Rajya Sabha holds two exclusive federal powers: Article 249 (legislating on State List in national interest) and Article 312 (creating new All-India Services).
• Exam Booster: Lok Sabha holds exclusive powers over Money Bills (Art 110) and No-Confidence Motions against the Council of Ministers (Art 75).
qe: Under Article 249 of the Indian Constitution, which House of Parliament enjoys the exclusive special power to authorize Parliament to legislate on a 'State List' subject in the national interest by a 2/3rd majority of members present and voting?

q: किस संवैधानिक अनुच्छेद के अंतर्गत उच्च न्यायालयों को न केवल मौलिक अधिकारों के प्रवर्तन के लिए बल्कि 'किसी अन्य प्रयोजन' के लिए भी रिट जारी करने की शक्ति प्राप्त है?
e:
Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs for both Fundamental Rights and ordinary legal rights ('any other purpose'), whereas Supreme Court's writ power under Article 32 applies strictly to Fundamental Rights.
• Exam Booster: Article 136 = Special Leave Petition (SLP) to Supreme Court; Article 227 = High Court's power of superintendence over subordinate courts.
qe: Under which Constitutional Article are High Courts empowered to issue writs not only for enforcing Fundamental Rights but also for 'any other purpose' (giving them a wider territorial-subject writ jurisdiction than the Supreme Court)?

q: सरकारिया आयोग की अनुशंसा पर 1990 में गठित 'अंतर्राज्यीय परिषद' (Inter-State Council) की स्थापना राष्ट्रपति द्वारा संविधान के किस अनुच्छेद के अंतर्गत की जाती है?
e:
Article 263 provides for the Inter-State Council (chaired by the Prime Minister, with Chief Ministers of all states and UTs).
• Exam Booster: Article 262 = Adjudication of inter-state river water disputes; Article 280 = Finance Commission.
qe: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the 'Inter-State Council' established by the President (constituted in 1990 on the recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission) to coordinate Centre–State policy?

q: भारत में किसी राज्य के राज्यपाल की नियुक्ति कौन करता है और राज्यपाल किसके प्रसादपर्यंत (pleasure) पद धारण करते हैं?
e:
Under Articles 155 and 156, the Governor is appointed by the President of India by warrant under his hand and seal, and holds office during the pleasure of the President (normal term 5 years).
• Exam Booster: Minimum age for Governor = 35 years; the 7th Constitutional Amendment (1956) allowed the same person to be appointed Governor for two or more states.
qe: Who appoints the Governor of a State in India, and during whose pleasure does the Governor hold office?
oe: Chief Justice of the High Court

q: भारत में किसी राज्य के राज्यपाल को पद की शपथ कौन दिलाता है?
o: संबंधित राज्य के उच्च न्यायालय के मुख्य न्यायाधीश
e:
Under Article 159, the oath of office to the Governor is administered by the Chief Justice of the High Court of that state (or the senior-most available judge).
• Exam Booster: Note the contrast: President appoints the Governor, but the High Court Chief Justice administers the Governor's oath!
qe: Who administers the oath of office to the Governor of a State in India?
oe: Chief Justice of the concerned State High Court

q: 73वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम (1992) के अंतर्गत पंचायती राज संस्थाओं के सभी स्तरों पर महिलाओं के लिए न्यूनतम कितने प्रतिशत सीटें आरक्षित हैं?
e:
Article 243D mandates at least one-third (33%) reservation for women in both seats and chairperson offices across all tiers of Panchayats (several states like Bihar, MP, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand have voluntarily raised it to 50%).
• Exam Booster: Article 243A defines 'Gram Sabha' (all registered voters in the village electoral roll).
qe: Under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992), what is the minimum percentage of seats reserved for women at all levels of Panchayati Raj Institutions?

q: किस संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम (1992) ने नगरीय स्थानीय निकायों (नगरपालिकाओं) को संवैधानिक दर्जा देने के लिए भाग IXA और बारहवीं अनुसूची (18 विषय) जोड़ी?
e:
The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 provides for three types of municipalities: Nagar Panchayat (transitional area), Municipal Council (smaller urban area), and Municipal Corporation (larger urban area).
• Exam Booster: Madras Municipal Corporation (1688) was India's first municipal corporation.
qe: Which Constitutional Amendment Act (1992) added Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule (18 functional items) to give constitutional status to Urban Local Bodies (Municipalities)?

q: भूरिया समिति की अनुशंसा पर पारित 'पेसा अधिनियम, 1996' (PESA Act) संशोधनों सहित भाग IX (पंचायतों) के प्रावधानों को किस अनुसूची के जनजातीय क्षेत्रों तक विस्तारित करता है?
e:
PESA Act, 1996 applies to the 10 Fifth Schedule states (Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, MP, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, Telangana), empowering Gram Sabhas over minor forest produce, land alienation, and minor minerals.
• Exam Booster: Part IX does NOT automatically apply to Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram, and Sixth Schedule tribal areas.
qe: The 'PESA Act, 1996' (Panchayats Extension to Scheduled Areas Act), enacted on the recommendation of the Bhuria Committee, extends the provisions of Part IX (Panchayats) with modifications to tribal areas listed in which Schedule?

q: सार्वजनिक प्राधिकरणों में पारदर्शिता और जवाबदेही को बढ़ावा देने हेतु भारतीय संसद ने ऐतिहासिक 'सूचना का अधिकार (RTI) अधिनियम' किस वर्ष पारित किया?
e:
The Right to Information Act was enacted in 2005 (came into full force on 12 October 2005), establishing the Central Information Commission (CIC) and State Information Commissions.
• Exam Booster: Under RTI, information must normally be provided within 30 days (and within 48 hours if it concerns the life or liberty of a person).
qe: In which year did the Indian Parliament enact the landmark 'Right to Information (RTI) Act' to promote transparency and accountability in public authorities?

q: मानवाधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम 1993 के अंतर्गत 12 अक्टूबर 1993 को स्थापित 'राष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार आयोग' (NHRC) किस प्रकार का निकाय है?
e:
NHRC is a STATUTORY (not constitutional) body created by an Act of Parliament; following the 2019 amendment, its Chairperson can be a former Chief Justice of India OR a former Judge of the Supreme Court (term 3 years or age 70).
• Exam Booster: International Human Rights Day is observed on 10 December (adoption of UDHR by UNGA in 1948).
qe: The 'National Human Rights Commission' (NHRC) of India, established on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, is what kind of body?

q: कौन-सा संवैधानिक प्रावधान भारत को एक 'पंथनिरपेक्ष राज्य' स्थापित करता है जहाँ राज्य का कोई आधिकारिक धर्म नहीं है और सभी व्यक्तियों को अंतःकरण एवं धर्म की समान स्वतंत्रता प्राप्त है?
e:
Articles 25–28 (Right to Freedom of Religion) together with the Preamble ('Secular') embody India's positive secularism ('Sarva Dharma Sambhava' — equal respect for all religions).
• Exam Booster: In S. R. Bommai vs Union of India (1994), the Supreme Court held that Secularism is an inviolable part of the Basic Structure of the Constitution.
qe: Which Constitutional provision establishes India as a 'Secular State' where the State has no official religion and grants equal freedom of conscience and religion to all persons?

q: दक्षेस (SAARC — 1985 में ढाका में स्थापित, 8 सदस्य राष्ट्र) का स्थायी सचिवालय कहाँ स्थित है?
e:
The SAARC Secretariat is located in Kathmandu, Nepal (established 1987). The 8 SAARC members are India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives, and Afghanistan (joined 2007).
• Exam Booster: BIMSTEC Secretariat is in Dhaka, Bangladesh; ASEAN Secretariat is in Jakarta, Indonesia; SCO Secretariat is in Beijing, China.
qe: Where is the permanent Secretariat of SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation, founded in Dhaka in 1985 with 8 member nations) located?

q: संयुक्त राष्ट्र के किस प्रमुख अंग को 'विश्व की लघु संसद' (Town Meeting of the World) कहा जाता है, जहाँ सभी 193 सदस्य राष्ट्रों को समान प्रतिनिधित्व (एक राष्ट्र, एक मत) प्राप्त है?
e:
The UN General Assembly (UNGA, HQ New York) is the main deliberative and policy-making organ of the UN; Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit of India became the first woman President of the UNGA in 1953.
• Exam Booster: The 6 principal organs of the UN: UNGA, UNSC, ECOSOC, Trusteeship Council (suspended 1994), ICJ (The Hague), and UN Secretariat.
qe: Which principal organ of the United Nations is known as the 'Town Meeting of the World' where all 193 member states have equal representation (one nation, one vote)?

q: 1998 के पोखरण-II परीक्षणों के बाद 2003 में औपचारिक रूप से अपनाया गया भारत का परमाणु सिद्धांत (Nuclear Doctrine) किन दो मूल सिद्धांतों पर आधारित है?
o: विश्वसनीय न्यूनतम प्रतिरोधक क्षमता और प्रथम प्रयोग न करना (No First Use)
पूर्वव्यापी प्रथम प्रहार और असीमित भंडार
नाटो के साथ संयुक्त परमाणु साझेदारी
e:
India's nuclear doctrine commits to 'Credible Minimum Deterrence', 'No First Use' (NFU), massive retaliation if attacked with nuclear weapons, and non-use against non-nuclear weapon states.
• Exam Booster: India conducted Pokhran-I ('Smiling Buddha') on 18 May 1974 and Pokhran-II ('Operation Shakti') on 11 & 13 May 1998 (National Technology Day = 11 May).
qe: India's Nuclear Doctrine (formally adopted in 2003 following the 1998 Pokhran-II tests) is anchored on which two core principles?
oe: Credible Minimum Deterrence and No First Use (NFU)
Pre-emptive First Strike and Unlimited Stockpile

q: किस संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम (2003) ने तत्कालीन राष्ट्रीय अनुसूचित जाति एवं जनजाति आयोग को दो पृथक संवैधानिक निकायों—NCSC (अनुच्छेद 338) और NCST (अनुच्छेद 338A)—में विभाजित किया?
e:
The 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 (effective 2004) created separate NCSC (Art 338) and NCST (Art 338A).
• Exam Booster: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act (2018) later gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) under Article 338B.
qe: Which Constitutional Amendment Act (2003) bifurcated the erstwhile National Commission for SCs and STs into two separate constitutional bodies—NCSC (Article 338) and NCST (Article 338A)?

q: जनप्रतिनिधित्व अधिनियम, 1951 की धारा 8(3) (लिली थॉमस बनाम भारत संघ, 2013 में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय द्वारा पुष्ट) के अंतर्गत किसी निर्वाचित सांसद या विधायक को कम से कम कितने वर्ष के कारावास की सजा होने पर तत्काल अयोग्य घोषित कर दिया जाता है?
e:
In Lily Thomas (2013), the Supreme Court struck down Section 8(4) and ruled that any MP/MLA convicted and sentenced to 2 years or more imprisonment is immediately disqualified from the date of conviction (plus 6 years post-release).
• Exam Booster: NOTA (None of the Above) option on EVMs was introduced following the PUCL vs Union of India judgment (2013).
qe: Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 (Section 8(3), upheld by the Supreme Court in Lily Thomas vs Union of India, 2013), an elected MP or MLA stands immediately disqualified upon conviction for an offence carrying imprisonment of at least:
